source.title: Why Fine-Tuning Encourages Hallucinations and How to Fix It
source.authors: Guy Kaplan; Zorik Gekhman; Zhen Zhu; Lotem Rozner; Yuval Reif; S. Swayamdipta; Derek Hoiem; Roy Schwartz

page_placements.theme: Interference in contextual retrieval, composition and forgetting

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures semantic overlap and interference in factual fine-tuning, but does not test sparse-feature superposition, polysemanticity, SAE features, or whether model features are one-dimensional directions. It cites Toy Models of Superposition but does not apply its method.
record.gate_note: The paper tests whether overlap among entity representations predicts factual forgetting. That is related to the claim’s subject, but it is not a test of the listed versions about feature superposition or polysemanticity. The rows below record those related results with versions ["none"]. Its discussion of capacity limitations concerns factual forgetting, not whether features compete for dimensions in the sense of V2.
record.test_reason: The study is about SFT-induced factual forgetting in Qwen2.5 and Llama. It measures entity-key cosine overlap and held-out accuracy loss. It cites Toy Models of Superposition once, for the remark that non-orthogonal keys let writes leak between stored facts. It never tests sparse-feature superposition (V1), whether polysemantic neurons arise from capacity pressure or otherwise (V2, V3), SAE or dictionary recovery (V4, V5), or feature dimensionality (V6). The overlap it measures is between whole entity representations, not superposed features. It also contrasts its account with a capacity limit on stored facts (Allen-Zhu & Li), not capacity in the V2 sense. So no row bears on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that SFT-induced hallucinations are factual forgetting driven mainly by interference among overlapping semantic representations, not by global capacity or behaviour cloning. Self-distillation mitigates this interference, and an associative-memory account predicts forgetting from key overlap. They also report that selective freezing or self-distillation cuts forgetting from about 15 pp to about 2 pp.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce or apply the Toy Models of Superposition method; it studies factual fine-tuning and entity-representation interference in LLMs.
record.method_sensitivity: Forgetting varies with synthetic-key type, dataset scale, and graded key overlap. The paper also reports that the magnitude of forgetting depends on self-distillation settings, including teacher snapshot, distillation weight, and temperature.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen2.5-1.5B synthetic fine-tuning, held-out forgetting tracks base-model key overlap with real cities. At 10^4 facts it is 2.1, 3.8, 7.2 and 10.3 pp across the four graded key types. At 10^6 facts, name-like keys cause 39 pp forgetting, while UUID keys stay at 0–4 pp at all scales.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interference from fine-tuning new facts grows with pre-existing representational overlap between new and stored entity keys, not with the number of facts alone.

fits_no_version.finding: At 10^6 facts, forgetting depends on key type (semantic 38–41 pp vs UUID 4 pp), not on value type.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entity-key overlap, not answer surface form, predicts factual forgetting in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Held-out entity hidden-state drift at layer 14 reaches about 11% under SFT on semantic keys. It stays near 5% under UUID-key SFT and under self-distillation on semantic keys.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overlap-induced representational drift accompanies factual forgetting, and output-space KL regularization suppresses it.

record.problems: The evidence concerns synthetic factual fine-tuning in the reported mechanism experiments, not sparse-feature superposition or polysemantic neurons. The paper reports no uncertainty estimates for the cited results. The associative-memory account is described as qualitative and uses idealizations; the authors note that some assumptions are violated in their experimental corpora.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results for the listed claim versions were left out. The rows record related entity-overlap, factual-forgetting, and representation-geometry findings only.

untested.parts: Toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, near-orthogonal overlapping directions, the sparsity-dependent transition, and regular geometry.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise from features competing for limited dimensions, with important features getting dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise for non-capacity reasons.
Whether LLM features spread across many neurons, or whether sparse features can be recovered by dictionary learning or SAEs.
Completeness, stability and canonicality of SAE features.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional or multi-dimensional.

record.verdict_notes: The only link to the original source is one citation (§5.3): non-orthogonal keys mean writes leak between facts. The study measures overlap directly, so its results neither rely on nor test superposition. Rows are correctly unlinked. Results come from Qwen2.5-1.5B only for §5. Main-pipeline replications on Qwen2.5-7B and Llama-3.1-8B (Appendix B) also have no bearing on the versions.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, sparse features exceeding dimensions, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometric arrangements.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise from limited representational capacity, and whether important features receive dedicated dimensions while others share.
Polysemantic neurons arising for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or sparse features can be recovered with a dictionary or SAE.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units of model representation.
Whether superposed features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.
